Class Matcher

java.lang.Object
easyIO.regexp.Matcher
public class Matcher extends Object
A matcher for a regular expression with captures. The matcher state is a skeleton RE whose positions are its top-level summands, plus a capture state: for each position, the set of capture environments of that summand. See notes2.txt.

  • Constructor Details

    • Matcher

      public Matcher(RegExp r)
      Create a matcher for r. Captures in r that do not have an index are numbered after any captures that do, in tree order: an enclosing capture before the captures inside it, and the parts of a concatenation from left to right. (The order of the alternatives of an alternation is not specified, so to control the numbering of captures in different alternatives, number them explicitly with Capture.capture(e, k) or Parser.parse.) Throws IllegalArgumentException if a capture occurs inside a Kleene star, or if two captures have the same index (as happens when combining patterns that were parsed separately with their captures numbered from 1).

    • match

      public List<Match> match(BacktrackScanner s) throws Matcher.FailedMatch
      All the ways the regular expression matches the entire input, in no particular order. Throws FailedMatch if there are none. The input is read lazily, one character at a time.
      Throws:
      Matcher.FailedMatch

    • matchPrefix

      public List<Match> matchPrefix(BacktrackScanner s, boolean captures) throws Matcher.FailedMatch
      The ways the longest prefix of the input, starting at the current position, matches the regular expression, possibly the empty prefix. The scanner is left just past the prefix. If captures is false, only recognition is done, which is faster, and the result is a single Match with no capture groups. Capture positions are relative to the start of the prefix. Throws FailedMatch if no prefix matches, leaving the input position unchanged. Finding the longest prefix may read past it; the scanner is rolled back to the end of the prefix.
      Throws:
      Matcher.FailedMatch

    • search

      public List<Match> search(BacktrackScanner s) throws Matcher.FailedMatch
      Find the first occurrence of the entire regular expression on the input. A mark is inserted at the beginning of the occurrence and the scanner position is left at the end of the longest string that matches the RE, so that the client can choose to accept or abort the match. All the ways the occurrence matches are returned, with capture positions relative to the start of the occurrence. Occurrences of the empty string are not found. If no occurrence is found, the scanner goes to the end of the input, no mark is left, and FailedMatch is thrown.
      Throws:
      Matcher.FailedMatch
